sources.notes: Regulator code of practice for electronic programme guides: information for viewers with hearing or visual impairments on using the guide, work with disability groups, broadcasters and set-top-box makers to improve usability, annual statements of improvements, prominence rules for public-service channels.

sources.title: Diary study of television planning and programme guides
sources.notes: Published usability research, CHI 2006 workshop: diary study of television planning; guide use is predominantly short-term now-and-next and evening planning, with reminders for programmes to watch or record; notes usability challenges of programme guides.

sources.title: The accessibility and usability of online job applications for screen reader users
sources.notes: Peer-reviewed usability study, 2023: three screen-reader users attempted full online job applications at 30 companies, 90 trials; 55.6% success rate, 76.7% of sites with at least one critical blocker; date pickers and option lists caused over a third of blockers; error messages unclear or hard to find; completion took 20 minutes to over two hours.

sources.title: Investigating the accessibility and usability of job application web sites for blind users
sources.notes: Peer-reviewed usability study, 2012: 16 screen-reader users, 32 application attempts at 16 companies; 28.1% completed independently; recommendations include accessible feedback, clear link text, structured layout, logical grouping of questions, clearly identified data formats and required fields.

sources.title: Using the Civil Service Jobs website as a candidate
sources.notes: Government employment-service guidance: candidate account, partially completed applications found under Applications, submitted applications cannot be changed, re-applying and withdrawal rules.

sources.title: Applying using our online recruitment application portal
sources.notes: Local-government guidance: a draft application can be saved at any time and returned to later, submitted applications cannot be edited, shortlisting is based on the form, anonymous shortlisting after the closing date.

sources.title: Contact their GP surgery online
sources.notes: Platform design-system pattern guidance, checked November 2026: contact a GP surgery online through a form or questionnaire; two routes — describe a health problem and receive the practice's decision on the next step, or book a directly available slot where the practice offers one; label the problem route by what the person does; replies arrive in the messages area; document requests sit in the same entry point; availability depends on the person's own practice.

sources.title: Learning analytics dashboards and student commitment in a large online course
sources.notes: Randomised trial in a credit-bearing online course with 8745 learners: dashboards combining clear low-inference visualisations with concise actionable feedback and visible pacing cues raised commitment, while a dashboard without feedback gave no measurable benefit; practice problems permitted three attempts with immediate automated feedback and detailed explanations after a correct answer or exhausted attempts.

sources.title: Design and evaluation of a learning analytics dashboard for students
sources.notes: Mixed-methods dashboard design and evaluation study with focus groups, think-aloud sessions, and a usability scale: students need reference frames to interpret progress data and a feedback box explaining the meaning and importance of the figures.

sources.title: Per-competency mastery scores versus aggregate scores in online learning
sources.notes: Formal mastery model: per-competency mastery scores separate genuine mastery from shallow point accumulation, while aggregate scores mask whether individual competencies are mastered.

sources.title: Queueing-network model of the Leitner spaced-repetition system
sources.notes: Peer-reviewed model of reviewing flashcards in the Leitner system: items the learner fails drop to a lower deck and are reviewed more often, with a sharp phase transition in learning outcomes as the rate of new-item introduction rises.

sources.title: Optimal reviewing schedule given by recall probability
sources.notes: Peer-reviewed study of the optimal reviewing schedule, given by the recall probability itself and validated in a large-scale natural experiment on a language-learning platform, where learners following the computed schedule memorised more effectively.

sources.title: Systematic assessment of popular commercial food apps for meal planning and shopping
sources.notes: Systematic assessment of 51 popular commercial food apps: meal planners and shopping lists were the most common features, and the conclusion is that future apps should combine meal planners, shopping lists, simple recipes, reminders and prompts, and food ordering to reduce the burden of the food provision pathway.

sources.title: User testing of commercial apps for family meals
sources.notes: Peer-reviewed user testing with 133 working parents over four-week trials: meal planners and shopping lists were used in the moment while the behaviour was occurring, and organisation was the key theme, with meal-planning apps and features promoting organisation found to be feasible, time-saving solutions.

sources.title: Content and quality analysis of free popular nutrition apps
sources.notes: Content and quality analysis of free popular nutrition apps: six apps offered customisable meal planning and eight created grocery lists from selected recipes.

sources.title: Overcoming roadblocks to healthy eating
sources.notes: Government health guidance for older adults: plan meals around what is on sale, create a shopping list in advance to stick to a budget, and use the list while shopping.

sources.title: Building a tool to make mail-in voter registration more accessible
sources.notes: Government guidance on a step-by-step mail-in voter registration form filler: state-specific progressive disclosure, inline state-specific help, screen-reader compatibility, adjustable display, missing-information prevention, duplicate-registration check, and automatic election-office address.

sources.title: Question pages pattern
sources.notes: Government service design pattern for one question per page: the page heading is the question, every page carries a back link, the forward control is labelled for continuing, each item is asked once, and not knowing is a valid answer.

sources.title: One thing per page
sources.notes: Government design guidance for one-question-per-page flows: easier for low-confidence users, works on small screens, and handles errors, branches, loops, and saving progress.

sources.title: Designing content and transactions for government services
sources.notes: Government service manual guidance on handling complex eligibility through routing questions inside the transaction, with a check-before-you-start step.

sources.title: Track your ballot
sources.notes: State election office ballot tracking: updates by email, text, or phone when the ballot is sent, received, accepted, or not accepted because of a signature problem that can be fixed within 21 days; tracking follows the envelope, not the vote.

sources.title: Ballot tracking
sources.notes: State election office ballot tracking: the date the ballot was sent and whether it was received, email sign-up for send and receive notifications and for registration updates and mail-ballot applications; ballots returned in person are not shown as received.

sources.title: Life cycle of a ballot
sources.notes: State election office life cycle of a ballot in ten steps: receive, mark, return, postmark deadline, collection, notification, signature verification, signature challenges, counting, and status check.

sources.title: How to know your vote counted
sources.notes: State election board guidance on ballot statuses: valid return, accepted, accepted after a cured signature problem, and accepted with an exception; the voter history records that a vote was cast, not how it was marked.

sources.title: Polling place lookup
sources.notes: State election office polling-place lookup: full address entry returns the election-day polling location plus early-voting dates, hours, and locations; registered voters can look up any time through the citizen portal.

sources.title: Find my polling place
sources.notes: State election commission polling-place finder: search by address, polling-place hours and directions, and address-refinement help when no match is found.

sources.title: Online voter registration accessibility report
sources.notes: Accessibility-organisation report on online voter registration: at the time only 1 of 20 state sites was fully accessible, with common barriers in inaccessible forms and screen-reader access, poor navigation, missing alt text, contrast, keyboard access, and tab order; also covers readability, languages, alternate registration routes, contact support, and accessibility statements.

sources.title: Respond to a jury summons
sources.notes: Court service guidance on responding to a jury summons: juror number and PIN printed on the letter with an example of where to find them, supporting documents for excusal and deferral, and a scam warning that a genuine summons is always sent by post and the service never asks for national ID numbers, bank details, or payment.

sources.title: Respond to your jury summons
sources.notes: State court guidance on responding to a jury summons: badge number plus PIN plus postcode sign-in, confirm, request disqualification, postpone, or request a hardship transfer, online at all hours, immediate confirmation for postponement and other requests answered within two business days.

sources.title: Reply to a jury summons
sources.notes: Government service for replying to a jury summons: reply within seven days, sign in with the juror number plus name and address exactly as shown on the letter, answers downloadable and saveable at the end, and a fine for not replying.

sources.title: Jury service
sources.notes: Government guidance on jury service: change of date by replying with reasons and suggesting three possible dates in the next twelve months, excusal by replying with reasons, and an appeal route.

sources.title: Juror resources
sources.notes: County court juror resources: the qualification questionnaire must be completed before requesting a deferral or excusal, first deferral online, and checking whether the juror number is called the day before.

sources.title: Automated jury information service
sources.notes: Court automated status line: enter the nine-digit participant number, call after 6:00 pm the day before reporting, directed to report or rescheduled, and postponement or excuse status available seven to ten business days after mailing.

sources.title: Juror call-in status
sources.notes: County court juror call-in status by group number: check on the Sunday evening before the start date, then twice daily during the term, and attend only if the group number has been called.

sources.title: Jury scams
sources.notes: Court scam warning: courts never require sensitive information in a phone call or email, most contact is by mail, and there are no requests for payment, fines, card numbers, or national ID numbers, and no warrant served by email, phone, or fax.

sources.title: Reply to a jury summons accessibility statement
sources.notes: Accessibility statement for the jury summons reply service: keyboard, screen reader, and speech recognition operation, zoom to 300 percent without text spilling, independently audited, and fully compliant with the current accessibility standard.

sources.title: Substitution policy in online grocery
sources.notes: Peer-reviewed retail study of substitution policy in online grocery: matching the dominant attribute for the category and matching past purchases raise substitution acceptance; two simulated-purchase experiments with more than 3,000 households across five categories.

sources.title: Fulfilment failures in online grocery
sources.notes: Peer-reviewed retail study of fulfilment failures in online grocery: failures delay the next order by 7.22 percent on average, and substitutions often make the delay and dissatisfaction worse rather than fixing it.

sources.title: Stock-out policy in online stores
sources.notes: Peer-reviewed retail study of stock-out policy in online stores: visible stock-outs with a suggested replacement facilitate substitution and slightly reduce cancellation, while stock-outs hidden until after a purchase attempt create confusion.

sources.title: Vaccinations National Booking Service
sources.notes: Government health-service booking service for vaccinations: online booking for eligible people with the number used to check eligibility and save the record, booking confirmation by text message or email, cancel and re-book where needed, and a phone route for people who cannot use the online service.

sources.title: National Vaccination Scheduling Service privacy notice
sources.notes: Government health-service portal for booking and rescheduling vaccination appointments, viewing vaccination history, and downloading a digital certificate or requesting a paper copy, with a phone helpline for people who do not use the portal.

sources.title: Using eHealth App to make COVID-19 Vaccination Booking
sources.notes: Government health-service page on booking vaccination through a health-record app: personal particulars and past vaccination records filled in automatically, records viewable in the app, and a handheld printout given after vaccination.

sources.title: Report: COVID Credential Design Criteria
sources.notes: Public-health report on vaccine credential design criteria: a scannable code as the quickest verification, privacy through codes that need not be human-readable, the code prominent for fast access, and three presentation scenarios — scanned at an establishment, scanned from a printed code, and additional information beyond the code.

sources.title: Self-service terminals and kiosks
sources.notes: Accessibility guidance for closed-environment terminals: multiple operating methods, spoken output through a personal headset with the screen blanked for privacy, tactile keys, time-limit warnings through more than one sense, and a simple predictable layout for first-time users.

sources.title: EAA Requirements for ATM Accessibility Software
sources.notes: Accessibility requirements for cash-machine software under the European accessibility framework: speech output, headset use, tactile keypad mapping, timing adjustments with extension, privacy mode for audio-assisted transactions, and multilingual options.

sources.title: Live-viewing apps
sources.notes: Platform guidance for live-viewing apps: feature live content prominently and mark it plainly apart from recorded titles, one-action playback, progress shown for programmes joined in progress, secondary actions in a fixed order, a content footer for browsing channels during playback that opens and closes by the same gesture, instant visible feedback on a channel change, and audio kept matched to the viewing context.

sources.title: A2UI 1.0: Build delightful, fast, reliable, agentic experiences
sources.notes: First stable version of an open protocol for agent-described screens: the agent describes the surface and each app renders it with its own native components from a registered catalogue, private values are bound on the server, live facts are checked through two-way calls, and accessibility support is included.

sources.title: The Public Charge Point Regulations 2023
sources.notes: Public charge point rules: rapid-charge networks must be reliable for 99% of the time on average across each calendar year, with compliance published; charge point data must be accurate and operational status updated in real time, and availability, location, connector type, payment methods and price must be openly available.

sources.title: Add a hotel room key to Apple Wallet on your iPhone
sources.notes: Platform support guidance for hotel room keys in a phone wallet: the key is added from the hotel app after booking, is added automatically to a paired watch, works by holding the device against the lock with Express Mode on by default, and is deactivated remotely when the stay ends.

sources.title: How to publish FAQs for Wallet-based Digital Keys in Mews Operations
sources.notes: Vendor help page recording the approved wallet-key wording: the key is added from an Add to Wallet button at the end of online check-in, activates only once check-in is complete and a room is assigned, works without waking or unlocking the device, keeps working for a stated time after the battery runs out on supported phones, and a physical key card remains available where the key cannot be added.

sources.title: Designing for watchOS
sources.notes: Platform design guidance for watch apps: quick, glanceable, single-screen interactions that deliver critical information succinctly and let people act with a simple gesture or two; minimal navigation depth with the Digital Crown for vertical navigation; haptic feedback consistent with the interaction's purpose; minimal time spent interacting with the app.

sources.title: Workouts
sources.notes: Platform design guidance for watchOS fitness apps: during an active workout show the data people are most likely to care about, such as elapsed or remaining time, calories burned, or distance travelled, with lap or interval markers; keep large session controls on their own screen and metrics on a dedicated screen readable at a glance; use a distinct appearance for an active workout; use large type and high contrast for reading in motion; avoid irrelevant information during a workout; provide a summary at the end of a session and discard extremely brief sessions. No prescribed field count, sport-specific view, or single-measure focus is stated.

sources.title: Principles of Wear OS development
sources.notes: Platform development guidance for watch apps: design for critical tasks only on the wrist, completable within seconds; a fitness app focuses on data gathering while detailed post-workout analysis stays on the phone; support offline use for exercise without the phone; keep long-lived activities visible through ongoing activity; confirm start, stop, auto-pause, and auto-lap with haptics; disable touch while tracking a workout to prevent accidental input.

sources.title: Flight Booking & Airlines research
sources.notes: Research library for flight booking: 120+ tested guidelines with benchmark scores and implementation examples across search, fare selection, booking checkout, accounts and loyalty; qualitative usability testing plus a 2026 quantitative study of 3,125 shoppers.

sources.title: Flight Booking & Airlines Quantitative UX Insights 2026
sources.notes: Three high-level findings from a 2026 survey of 3,125 shoppers: travellers search across several sources with airline sites most used; 78% belong to at least one loyalty programme; business travellers bundle hotels, cars, insurance and parking more often than leisure travellers; search discoverability and suggestions, clear comparable pricing, visible loyalty balances and contextual bundling follow from the findings.

sources.title: Handbook for VVSG 2.0 Usability and Accessibility Test Strategies
sources.notes: Test strategies for the usability and accessibility requirements in the voting system guidelines: text size and contrast, scrolling and gestures, plain language, and testing with voters; electronic text sizes from 3.5 mm to 25 mm with a larger default than the earlier version, and no horizontal scrolling or panning when zoomed to 200%.

sources.title: Applying VVSG 2.0 requirements to remote ballot marking systems
sources.notes: How the voting system guidelines apply to remote ballot marking: default electronic text size 4.8 mm with a range of 3.5 mm to 9.0 mm, sans-serif text, touch areas at least 12.7 mm with 2.54 mm between them, plain language, and the same functions in every display format and interaction mode with settings and selections preserved across a format switch.

sources.title: Field Guide Vol. 01: Designing usable ballots
sources.notes: Ten design tips for usable ballots from the field guides to ensuring voter intent: readable type, consistent marking spaces, clearly separated contests in a single column, instructions at the start in plain language, and a review step before casting.

sources.title: Evaluating Rich Visual Feedback on Head-Up Displays for In-Vehicle Voice Assistants: A User Study
sources.notes: Thirty-two participants compared three head-up display designs for in-vehicle voice assistant feedback: a minimal design showing essential keywords only scored highest on usability, and a layered augmented-reality design outperformed a flat scrolling list; distraction effects were not statistically significant.

sources.title: Visual Feedback for In-Car Voice
sources.notes: Ambient colour feedback for an in-car voice assistant, evaluated by survey (151 respondents) and a lab study (24 participants): most participants preferred the ambient feedback over conventional or no visual feedback, with higher visibility and usefulness ratings, while auditory cues remained necessary; also notes the 2026 safety-rating rules for in-car interfaces.

sources.title: 14 Budget App Dashboard Design Examples
sources.notes: Fourteen recorded budget dashboard screens: a useful dashboard explains the period, available amount, plan, actual spending, and the action that changes the outcome; start with period, currency, method, and one meaningful object; charts as navigational summaries with labelled values and drill-down; category budget cards with monthly amount, daily equivalent, actual spending, and percentage.

sources.title: Data visualization guidelines - CFPB Design System
sources.notes: Choose the chart by what it must communicate: bars for comparisons of discrete items, lines for change over time with the axis starting at zero, pie slices adding to 100 percent; limit the number of data types in one chart; label every value and never carry meaning by colour alone.

sources.title: BGA Studio Guidelines (UX/UI)
sources.notes: Platform guidelines for board game adaptations: the game should fit a square ratio showing everything the active player needs, centred on all devices, with a no-action margin around the board; never hide game components behind popups; the action bar shows the current state with at most four buttons plus context and never replaces a board action; player panels stay compact, at most a quarter of a phone screen for four players; the game is fully playable at full scale with no zoom controls; interactive elements are at least 32 by 32 px; text meets the standard contrast minimum; regular animations stay at half a second, at most eight tenths; tooltips add insight rather than duplicating; the whole game is playable with single clicks; a game log records each move; fidelity to the original game is an absolute requirement.

sources.title: Art Direction and User Interface
sources.notes: Publisher guide for taking a board game to the digital space: separate out-of-game screens from in-game screens, map every screen and its connections before designing, place interface elements shared across screens always in the same place, build a consistent library of elements, keep the layout usable from phone to desktop, and leave room for longer translated text, with French about 30 percent longer and German about 50 percent longer than English.

sources.title: Child-Centered User Interface Design for Early Language Learning Applications: A Qualitative Comparative Study
sources.notes: Peer-reviewed 2026 qualitative comparative study of early language learning applications: intuitive minimal-step navigation reduces cognitive load and supports task completion; balanced colour sustains attention without overstimulation; large plain typography improves reading accuracy; expressive mascots support emotional engagement; preferences vary across developmental stages, so the interface should adapt rather than standardise.

sources.title: Language Learning App UI Template
sources.notes: Wireframe template for a gamified language learning app: placement onboarding asking why the learner is learning and their level, a lesson path of labelled sections and units, three exercise types (translate with a word bank, tap matching pairs, true-or-false on a short dialogue), one shared exercise frame with a progress bar and a single bottom button reading Check before answering and Continue after, a lesson-complete screen showing points, accuracy and time, and streak and quest views.

sources.title: UI/UX Design for Learning Apps: Complete Guide
sources.notes: Guide to learning-app interface design: chunk information into small units to manage cognitive load, keep short focused lessons of three to seven minutes, show progress bars and milestones so progress stays visible, and align the interface with spaced repetition, scaffolding, and active recall.

sources.title: Set up Apple Pay
sources.notes: Official platform guidance for adding a card to a wallet: prerequisites of a compatible device, a supported card from a participating issuer, a signed-in account, and a device check set; add by tapping the card on the phone, scanning it in the frame, or entering the details by hand; issuer verification before the card is usable; adding the card to a paired watch; and removal from all devices.

sources.title: Fix problems with tap to pay transactions
sources.notes: Official platform help for tap-to-pay setup: check the device supports NFC and switch it on, set the wallet as the default payment app, add a card by camera or manual entry, accept the issuer terms, verify the card when asked, keep a screen lock set, and check tap-to-pay readiness in the wallet.

sources.title: Customize playback controls
sources.notes: Platform design guidance for media apps: the playback view and the queue — show thumbnails, a now-playing indicator and previously played items in the queue, keep custom actions consistent, and use text at the largest readable size inside icons.

sources.title: Playback view
sources.notes: Platform design guidance for the media playback view: metadata with elapsed time, a queue button, playback controls with a visual progress indicator, primary actions in the order queue, previous, play or pause, next, and secondary actions behind an overflow control.

sources.title: Wallet Developer Guide: Pass Design and Creation
sources.notes: Official platform developer guidance for designing wallet passes: pass styles for boarding passes, store cards, coupons, event tickets and generic passes; field layout set by the style; barcode use; and designing for every device including a paired watch.

sources.title: Getting Started with Apple Wallet
sources.notes: Official platform guidance for wallet passes: choose the pass style that matches the use, keep passes clear and readable on all devices, and use barcodes for scanning.

sources.title: Carbon components v0.114.0 release notes
sources.notes: Release notes for the current major line: renamed tokens, full right-to-left mirroring, a layer system replacing the light prop, a built-in calendar date picker, and 25 new components including a chat set and a content-labelling component.

sources.title: Joint Statement on Suspicious Activity Report Confidentiality Considerations Regarding Communications with Customers
sources.notes: A bank may discuss the underlying facts of a suspicious transaction — dates, amounts, parties — with the customer, notify them that a delay, limitation, restriction or closure may relate to suspected fraud, ask about the purpose of a transaction or the source of funds, and provide fraud warnings; it must never reveal that a report exists or that a transaction has been reported.

sources.title: Draft Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Third Amendment Directions, 2026
sources.notes: Draft directions, March 2026, to apply from 1 July 2026: instant text alerts for electronic transactions above ₹500 and email alerts wherever an address is held, in addition to push alerts; a number to text an objection to, carried in the alert itself; round-the-clock multi-channel fraud reporting; immediate acknowledgement with a complaint number and timestamp; immediate steps to prevent further unauthorised transactions; a response within 30 days including reversal details.

sources.title: Building a patient portal for secondary care bookings
sources.notes: Patient portal guide: mobile-first layout, sign-in to a high assurance level, view, cancel and reschedule appointments as separate journeys, pending states shown until a request is fulfilled, and deep links to a specific appointment.

sources.title: Proxy access
sources.notes: Formal proxy access: the proxy has their own account and credentials, a level of access tailored to the person's wishes and different per proxy, explicit consent with a coercion check, sensitive information redacted, withdrawal at the person's request without affecting their own access, and routine review.

sources.title: From Immediate Access to Meaningful Delivery: A Patient-Centered Approach to Delivering Test Results
sources.notes: Only 66% of patients who saw results early understood what they meant, and only 28% were given a choice in how and when results were released; plain-language explanations belong beside the result, sensitive results may be delayed until a clinician has spoken to the patient, and release preferences should be honoured rather than defaulting to immediate alerts.

sources.title: Manage a session timeout
sources.notes: Warn at least 2 minutes before a session times out, in a dialog that lets the person stay in the service and keep their work; if nothing is done, redirect to a timeout page that explains what happened and how to continue. Meets the extend condition of the timing-adjustable criterion.

sources.title: Media Session
sources.notes: The web standard for describing playing media to the platform: title, artist, album and artwork metadata; playback state and position state so lock screens and notification shades show a scrubber; and action handlers for play, pause, seek backward and forward, previous and next track, and seek to a position, answered from lock screens, headset buttons, and keyboard media keys.

sources.title: MediaSession
sources.notes: Reference documentation for the media session interface: metadata for display in platform playback controls, playback state, action handlers, and position reporting.

sources.title: Podcast player, the controls your listeners expect
sources.notes: Podcast player controls as settled in practice: skip back 15 seconds and forward 30 seconds, changeable from 10 to 60 seconds in steps of 5; playback speed from 0.5x to 3x in steps of 0.1; a sleep timer with 5, 10, 15, 30 and 45 minutes, 1 hour, and end of episode; resume from the stored position with time left shown in lists.

sources.title: Audiobooks
sources.notes: The audiobook profile of the publication manifest: a collection of audio resources grouped by a reading order with metadata and resources; duration stated for the whole book and per item in the reading order; a table of contents reflecting the structural outline of the book; cover and supplemental resources carried in the manifest.

sources.title: The ANUK/Unipol Code of Standards for Larger Developments
sources.notes: National code of practice for larger student developments, approved 27 February 2026: standards for building condition and fire safety, repairs within agreed timescales, deposits, and a complaints process with independent external input; membership is voluntary and is the test of compliance.

sources.title: Accommodation FAQ
sources.notes: University accommodation guidance: an advance rent payment completes the booking; guarantor requirements are stated in the offer before acceptance; residences are accredited under the national code of practice for larger student developments.

sources.title: Halls or Housemates? The UK Student Housing Choice That Shapes Your First Year
sources.notes: Student housing choices and costs: halls, private blocks, and shared houses; rent as a share of the monthly budget; bills, a deposit of up to five weeks' rent, and the first month's rent due with the keys; start looking three to four months before arrival.

sources.title: Passkey Authentication | Modern Web Guidance | Chrome for Developers
sources.notes: Returning-user sign-in with discoverable credentials through an explicit control and through browser autofill suggestions; detect support for the autofill route first and keep the explicit control where autofill is unavailable; passwords stay available alongside passkeys.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2021/782 on rail passengers' rights and obligations
sources.notes: Pre-purchase information: timetables, conditions for all available fares highlighting the lowest, first and second class seating availability, planned and real-time disruptions and delays, and whether the ticket is a through-ticket; tickets and reservations offered including sale over the internet; where a delay of 60 minutes or more is expected, reimbursement, re-routing at the earliest opportunity, or re-routing at a later date.

sources.title: Advance Tickets Terms and Conditions
sources.notes: An advance ticket is valid only on the date and train shown, and the traveller must travel in the class and reserved seat shown on the ticket; changes to time or date must be arranged before departure of the first reserved train, origin, destination and operator staying the same, with a fee plus any fare difference payable; the ticket is non-refundable except where the train is cancelled or delayed and the traveller chooses not to travel.

sources.title: Can I hold a train ticket before booking?
sources.notes: Reservations are put on hold when added to the basket and held until bought or they expire; hold length varies by operator and fare type and is shown when added; the price is fixed during the hold and seat reservations are guaranteed; held items can be deleted at any time; once the time is up the tickets disappear from the basket and must be booked again.

sources.title: New Fare Payment Systems and Payment Technology: Best Practices and Recommendations
sources.notes: Decide the validation type up front, visual validation or a validator; anti-fraud measures such as unique ticket branding, scrolling images, or specific colours; establish a policy to allow riders to board without requiring cellular service to activate; mobile ticketing rated straightforward for passes, zonal and distance-based fares, and fare capping.

sources.title: Which transport tickets are available on telephones
sources.notes: Ticket choice before payment: ticket type, full or reduced fare, zones and dates selected at purchase; incompatible tickets cannot coexist on one medium; a valid pass suppresses other ticket offers to avoid duplicates; passes take priority over single tickets on their day of validity.

sources.title: How to validate with my telephone
sources.notes: Travel is limited to the dates and zones selected at purchase; validation needs NFC on and the screen on, usually without opening the app; after several days offline, validation may fail and the app must alert the rider to reconnect.

sources.title: Transit passes: QR code entry points
sources.notes: Tickets bought in-app or on a mobile web flow can be saved to the system wallet as static QR or dynamic-code passes; the purchase flow must be mobile-optimised, support a wallet payment method, and offer the save-to-wallet step immediately after purchase; passes carry expiry state so expired passes are hidden, and a scannable code is presented at full brightness for inspection.

sources.title: Guidelines on Digital Mental Health Applications
sources.notes: Crisis helpline numbers, SOS buttons and emergency resource links prominent, visible across key sections, accessible at all times, with minimal steps including one-click calling, and numbers periodically verified; graded, sensitive nudging to seek professional help when high distress is detected; data minimisation, plain-language disclosure of what is collected and where it is stored, retention and deletion, easy account and data deletion, dynamic consent; diagnostic terms used cautiously, never as a definitive label; the app states plainly it is not a substitute for diagnosis, therapy, or emergency services.

sources.title: NHS service standard
sources.notes: Build a service that is simple to use so people can succeed first time; understand users' clinical, practical and emotional needs; create a secure service which protects privacy; actively manage safety risks; make sure everyone can use the service, including people with different mental health, learning, social and cultural needs.

sources.title: Evidence Standards Framework for digital health technologies
sources.notes: Intended-user-group acceptability incorporated in design; intended purpose and target population described; good data practices embedded in design; safeguarding assurances where users are in vulnerable groups; level of professional oversight defined; evidence of effectiveness required for claimed benefits.

sources.title: Period Tracking App Privacy: What Cycle Apps Collect and Who Sees It
sources.notes: Cycle apps collect cycle dates, symptoms, moods, sexual activity, pregnancy status and test results; the 2024 amendments to the Health Breach Notification Rule name fertility and sexual health apps explicitly, and treat an unauthorised disclosure — including health data passed to analytics or advertising kits — as a breach; data kept only on the device or end-to-end encrypted is reachable mainly through the device.

sources.title: App Store Guideline 5.1.3: No Health Data for Ads or iCloud
sources.notes: Quotes the platform review guideline for health data: health, fitness, and medical data may not be used or disclosed to third parties for advertising, marketing, or other use-based data mining; false or inaccurate data must not be written into the health store; personal health information must not be stored in the cloud; the specific health data collected from the device must be disclosed.

sources.title: Priority Pass — airport lounge membership app redesign
sources.notes: Shipped redesign of a lounge membership app: the digital pass with a clear hierarchy for membership status, expiry, and scannable code, layouts optimised for scanning at lounge entrances, key assets cached locally for offline use in airports with weak connectivity, scalable patterns for members with multiple cards, and design for failure as the guiding constraint.

sources.title: Mobile Wallet Reference
sources.notes: Documents the wallet pass field model — header, primary, secondary, and auxiliary fields — and the platform pass design guides: a generic pass suits membership cards and access badges, a store card suits loyalty and gift cards; passes show relevance information on the lock screen and support QR, Aztec, and barcode formats.

sources.title: Enroll in the Visa Airport Companion program
sources.notes: Enrolment in a lounge programme through the companion app; entry by presenting the digital membership card and QR code in the app, from the welcome email, or with the enrolled card; access to lounges is always subject to availability and lounge discretion.

sources.title: Thermostat - Matter Survey
sources.notes: The open standard's thermostat cluster: local temperature, setpoint limits, system mode, running mode, start of week, setpoint hold duration, programming operation mode, setpoint presets, events, and enhanced schedules; mandatory for thermostat device types.

sources.title: Simplifying smart temperature control — Nest thermostat redesign
sources.notes: Redesign of a thermostat ecosystem: one target temperature with the system choosing heat or cool, no separate heating and cooling thresholds; system state — current temperature, active mode, eco status — first in the hierarchy; a vertical schedule timeline replacing a horizontal drag timeline; named schedule events applied across days; the same interaction logic on the wall device and the phone.

sources.title: Matter Protocol and HVAC: How the Universal Smart Home Standard Connects Thermostats, Sensors, and HVAC Systems
sources.notes: The open smart-home standard lets one thermostat work across platforms without manufacturer lock-in; the thermostat device type has been supported since the first version of the standard; Matter 1.6 added smarter thermostat capabilities; the standard exposes current temperature, setpoint, heat, cool, and auto mode, while learning schedules, room sensors, and energy reports usually stay in the maker's app.

sources.title: WebMCP implementation guide
sources.notes: Browser tool registration for in-browser agents: the document entry point, the origin trial, the testing panel, and authorisation before tools run.

sources.title: What is WebMCP?
sources.notes: Draft community-group proposal, trial versions, the entry-point move from navigator to document, and storefront use with tools switched on by default.

sources.title: WebMCP guide: connecting tools to browser agents
sources.notes: Draft status, the current entry point, and registering named tools with a description and a schema.

sources.title: What is WebMCP, and how to track which websites adopt it
sources.notes: Draft history, the two registration forms, the entry-point move, and how the proposal differs from the wider protocol.

sources.title: What is WebMCP? How a new browser feature lets agents use websites
sources.notes: Trial versions, the testing flag, and the document entry point for tool registration.

sources.title: Why a general calendar fails for families
sources.notes: Household-first design: one colour per person, a shared canvas instead of one owner, and a wall display mode.

sources.title: Why a colour-coded family calendar changes everything
sources.notes: Per-member colour carried across week, agenda, and widget views; choosing colours that stay distinct.

sources.title: How to set up a colour-coded family calendar
sources.notes: One colour per person forever, a neutral colour for shared events, accessible palettes, and the wall display.

sources.title: Calendar colours and visibility
sources.notes: Per-calendar colours, side-by-side columns in shared slots, and a family-hub colour system with one colour per person.

sources.title: How to build a colour-coded family calendar that everyone actually uses
sources.notes: Colour by person, not by category; one colour per person forever; a separate colour for family-wide events.

sources.title: User experience design for consumer-to-consumer platforms
sources.notes: Dual buyer and seller journeys, listing friction, pricing suggestions, and transaction milestones from listing to review.

sources.title: Marketplace app design template
sources.notes: Two-sided marketplace wireframes: search, item detail with protection fees, the sell flow, offers, chat, and checkout.

sources.title: Marketplace app interface design
sources.notes: Dual-sided navigation, trust as a first-class element, listing quality, and fee disclosure before purchase.

sources.title: Marketplace web interface architect
sources.notes: Listing creation, listing states from draft to removed, seller dashboards, and trust signals on the item page.

sources.title: Trust and ease of use on peer-to-peer marketplaces
sources.notes: Verified profiles, listing quality, authentic visuals, and questions on listings before purchase.

sources.title: Signaling One-Click Functionality for List Email Headers
sources.notes: One-click unsubscribe mechanism: the List-Unsubscribe header carries one HTTPS address and the List-Unsubscribe-Post header carries List-Unsubscribe=One-Click, so the mailbox provider can offer an unsubscribe control and send a POST that the sender honours without further action from the recipient; a valid DKIM signature must cover both headers.

sources.title: Email Unsubscribe Best Practices: The Legal and Smart Way
sources.notes: Bulk senders above 5,000 messages a day must offer one-click unsubscribe honoured within two days; the body link uses the word unsubscribe, stays visible, and needs no sign-in or survey before the request is honoured; confirmation happens on a page rather than by another email; a preference centre offers frequency, topic, and pause choices beside the full unsubscribe.

sources.title: Menu Labeling Requirements
sources.notes: Chains of 20 or more locations must show calories for standard items on menus and menu boards and for self-service foods close to the item, display the 2,000-calorie daily-intake statement and the additional-nutrition-on-request statement, and provide full written nutrition information on request.

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
sources.notes: Pointer targets at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, text contrast at least 4.5:1, text resizable to 200%, and time limits that can be extended or warned about.

sources.title: Digital Services Act, Article 27 — Recommender system transparency
sources.notes: Recommender systems must state in plain language the main parameters used and their relative importance, explain why specific information is suggested, and offer a control to modify those parameters directly and easily accessible from the section where the information is prioritised; very large platforms must offer at least one option not based on profiling.

sources.title: Set up parental controls to manage your child's iPhone or iPad
sources.notes: Separate child account in a family group, age-based defaults, approval flows for apps, purchases and websites decided from the guardian's own device, allowed and blocked lists, time allowances per app category, school, weekday and weekend schedules with a pause control, content restrictions by age rating, and a passcode gating settings changes.

sources.title: Age Appropriate Design: A Code of Practice for Online Services — Code standards
sources.notes: Fifteen standards for services likely to be accessed by children, including age-appropriate application, high privacy by default, data minimisation, and parental controls that give the child age-appropriate information and show an obvious sign when activity or location is monitored.

sources.title: Unfair commercial practices
sources.notes: Property for sale or lease is a product, so a listing with a price is an invitation to purchase; omitting material information is always unfair, the total price must include all mandatory charges with drip pricing prohibited, and fake reviews and misuse of trust marks are banned in all circumstances.

sources.title: DoorLock trait — Matter standard reference
sources.notes: Per-user PIN credentials, a user database, weekday and year-day access schedules, on-lock logging, credentials sent over the air, and operation and programming notifications.

sources.title: Cyber Security for Consumer IoT: Baseline Requirements (ETSI EN 303 645)
sources.notes: Provision table: passwords unique per device or user-defined, a simple mechanism to change the authentication value, brute-force protection, and network access and security-relevant configuration changes only after authentication.

sources.title: Regulations: consumer connectable product security
sources.notes: Baseline security requirements for consumer connectable products, including a ban on universal default passwords, aligned with the consumer IoT baseline standard.

sources.title: Securing Your Internet-Connected Devices at Home
sources.notes: Change default credentials, use two-factor authentication where offered, and disable remote management that is not used.

sources.title: Guidelines for Safety of Women Passengers Using App-Based and Digital Transport Mobility Services
sources.notes: Verbatim reproduction of the full guidelines text; the commission's own site copy was not located in search. Driver and vehicle must match the app display with penalty-free cancellation on mismatch, no unauthorised passenger may be added to a pooled ride, verified co-passenger details may be shown, route deviations and long stops raise real-time alerts, and grievance acknowledgement within 2 hours with resolution within 72 hours.

sources.title: Motor Vehicles Aggregators Rules
sources.notes: Ride pooling permitted for riders travelling along the same route, passengers may choose to pool only with other women, cancellation without valid reason incurs a penalty of 10% of the fare capped at Rs. 100, and apps must offer live location sharing and 24x7 call centres.

sources.title: Maharashtra aggregator policy — carpooling recognition
sources.notes: Gives legal recognition to carpooling, allows cost-sharing among passengers, and prohibits private vehicle owners from earning a profit.

sources.title: Human Interface Guidelines — Materials
sources.notes: Platform guidance for the translucent refractive control-layer material: reserved for the navigation and control layer floating above content (tab bars, toolbars, sidebars, buttons), never in the content layer; regular and clear variants; controls shrink or simplify on scroll; legibility over scrolling content and a user clarity control.

sources.title: Track workouts with HealthKit on iOS and iPadOS
sources.notes: Platform session on phone-side workout tracking: a three-second countdown before start so sensors connect, the start, pause, resume, and end lifecycle, live figures on the lock screen with duration only where health data is unavailable, voice-assistant start, pause, resume, and cancel without unlocking, heart rate only from a paired external sensor, crash recovery that restores the session, and post-workout summaries from saved workout statistics.

sources.title: Loyalty cards | Google for Developers
sources.notes: Wallet pass development flow for loyalty cards: a class defines the properties shared across passes, an object defines the pass for one person, and the issued pass is delivered with an add-to-wallet button or link.

sources.title: Create Passes Classes and Passes Objects | Loyalty cards
sources.notes: Creating loyalty classes and objects: the class is the template for a programme, the object is the per-person pass, created through the wallet API or the business console.

sources.title: Update Passes Classes and Passes Objects | Loyalty cards
sources.notes: Keeping loyalty passes current: updating a class affects all holders, updating an object affects one person, with a full update or a patch of changed fields, and regular updates recommended so the pass reflects balance and tier changes.

sources.title: NHS Talking Therapies for anxiety and depression
sources.notes: Talking therapies access: self-referral into every service, a choice of in-person or remote delivery by phone, video, or online, guided programmes with practitioner support, therapies matched to the difficulty, and session-by-session outcome monitoring.

sources.title: FetchAid: Making Parcel Lockers More Accessible to Blind and Low Vision People
sources.notes: Peer-reviewed locker accessibility study: fingertip and button detection on the locker touchscreen guides the person to reveal and scan the QR code, then audio guidance leads to the compartment door, with an error-recovery mechanism and real-time feedback; 12 blind and low-vision participants completed pickups faster with less effort and frustration.

sources.title: Accessibility in parcel logistics: What the EAA means for parcel lockers
sources.notes: European Accessibility Act and EN 301 549 require parcel stations to present information in more than one sensory channel: tactile elements, a speaker with audio guidance, and a guide to the box by audio signal or light; grip heights for ICT products follow EN 301 549.

sources.title: ADA & EN 301 549 Kiosk Compliance Explained
sources.notes: Public kiosks must be operable from a wheelchair, by a blind person, and with limited hand strength: reach range 15 to 48 inches, 4.5:1 contrast, speech output with private listening through a headphone jack, and tactile or audible alternatives to touch-only controls; the practical build is a hybrid of touchscreen, tactile keypad, and speech output.

sources.title: Kiosk Accessibility Standards: CSA B651.2, ADA
sources.notes: CSA/ASC B651.2:25 requires every function of a self-service device in visual text and audible speech, with volume control, a headphone jack, tactile input, and at least one mode operable with one hand without tight grasping, pinching, or twisting; an accessible enclosure running an inaccessible application is still an inaccessible kiosk.

sources.title: Proposal for a Regulation: EU KIDS Act (COM(2026) 681 final)
sources.notes: Commission proposal adopted 17 September 2026; graduated account ages under 13, 13 to 14 supervised, 15 and over; safety-by-design defaults for all until age assurance establishes adulthood; typed age excluded as a check; not yet adopted law.

sources.title: EU KIDS Act: helping children navigate a safer online world
sources.notes: Official summary: gradual uptake of social media for children; proposal now examined by the Parliament and the Council before it becomes law.

sources.title: Guidelines on measures to ensure a high level of privacy, safety and security for minors online
sources.notes: Adopted 14 July 2025 under DSA Article 28(4); minors' accounts private by default, age assurance accurate, reliable, robust, non-intrusive and non-discriminatory, features encouraging excessive use disabled by default.

sources.title: Statement 1/2025 on Age Assurance
sources.notes: Ten principles for age assurance; risk-based, proportionate and data-minimising; threshold-only answers where a range suffices; typed age unlikely to be robust.

sources.title: U-space
sources.notes: Regulator framework for unmanned traffic management; mandatory services are flight authorisation, geo-awareness, network identification and traffic information; operator-facing, not consumer tracking.

sources.title: Package Delivery by Drone (Part 135)
sources.notes: Regulator page on certification of delivery operators; flights under 400 feet; no consumer tracking interface guidance.

sources.title: CarPlay Developer Guide
sources.notes: Quick food ordering rules: simplified ordering only, recent orders or favourites limited to 12 items, store selection and order confirmation; category covers drive-through and pickup ordering, not general retail curbside pickup.

sources.title: UI/UX Design of Laundry Pick-Up and Delivery Application using Prototyping Method
sources.notes: Prototyping study of a laundry pickup and delivery application: order tracking, automatic cost calculation based on weight, service assessment module; covers scheduling, weight-based pricing and staged tracking, not per-item inventory, wash preferences, delivery window, or damage reporting.

sources.title: Introduction to ticketing for museums and galleries
sources.notes: Sector-body guide to introducing timed entry booking: timed sessions across dates and times, simple registration, pre-defined capacity numbers, late-arrival rule with 10-minute arrival and possible non-admittance, accessibility and companion tickets per slot, walk-in allocation, rules communicated on site, tickets and confirmation emails.

sources.title: Museums, tourism and crowds
sources.notes: 2019 university thesis, comparative case study of two museums: time-slotted online tickets spread visitors through the day and reduced queues, with reduced maximum capacity improving the visit.

sources.title: Material Design 3
sources.notes: Expressive guidance: 14 new or updated components, token-driven motion physics, 35-shape library with shape morphing, updated design kit; Compose-first direction.

sources.title: Compose Material 3 release notes
sources.notes: Stable 1.5.0 with Compose 1.13, released 18 November 2026; motion scheme, wavy progress indicators and expressive theme promoted during the 1.5.0 alpha series.

sources.title: Gmail Material 3 Expressive settings redesign starts rolling out
sources.notes: Settings interface restyled with rounded cards, expressive switches and colour-coded icons, with writing settings grouped under one heading; rollout server-side and limited.

sources.title: Gmail's Settings Page Is Getting a Colorful Material 3 Expressive Makeover
sources.notes: Corroborates the Gmail settings redesign: rounded cards, redesigned switches, grouped writing settings; server-side rollout with unclear coverage.

sources.title: Q2 & Q3 2026 Recap
sources.notes: Chakra UI v3.38.0 shipped 3 November 2026 with a Command component for searchable command menus; FloatingPanel and DateInput landed earlier in 2026.

sources.title: Appliance remote control
sources.notes: Safety-gated remote control: appliance safety standards such as the IEC 60335 family, remote start armed locally at the appliance and cancelled when the door opens, remote switch-off almost always allowed, heat sources most restricted, remote control as a convenience layer over full local operation.

sources.title: Control Your Washing Machine Remotely with wifi
sources.notes: Vendor account of smart washer control: remote start and pause, live cycle monitoring, saved custom programmes, finish-by scheduling in off-peak hours, completion and maintenance notices.

sources.title: Washing Machine User Manual — Remote Control Function
sources.notes: Manufacturer manual: remote control set up by holding the on/off and remote-control keys at the appliance, status notices at the end of a programme, all safety measures applying to remote operation.

sources.title: Open311 GeoReport v2
sources.notes: Frozen and finalised specification for reporting location-based non-emergency issues: service list with codes, groups and metadata, per-service definitions with required fields in stated order, location as coordinates, address text or address identifier, media by reference, reference number or token, open or closed status with notes, 4,000-character description, optional contact fields, ISO 8601 dates, HTTPS.

sources.title: European legislation on eInvoicing
sources.notes: Directive 2014/55/EU and the EN 16931 standard define the common semantic data model for electronic invoices; public contracting authorities must receive and process compliant invoices.

sources.title: Peppol BIS Billing 3.0
sources.notes: Core Invoice Usage Specification of EN 16931: invoice processes including pre-payment and payment in advance, payment means and instructions, pre-payment settled through a final invoice, buyer reference, credit notes for corrections.

sources.title: Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 business rules
sources.notes: Business rules for the billing profile: partial-invoice document type code 326 for milestone billing, mandatory buyer reference and electronic addresses.

sources.title: Invoices: what they must include
sources.notes: Government guidance on invoice content: unique number, issue date, seller and buyer identity, line items with quantity and unit price, tax breakdown, totals.

sources.title: Factur-X 1.08 / ZUGFeRD 2.4
sources.notes: Hybrid invoice format, EN 16931-compliant: a human-readable PDF carrying the full structured invoice data embedded as XML, so one file serves both human reading and machine processing.

sources.title: Financial promotions for high-risk investments: multi-firm review
sources.notes: Regulator review of high-risk investment promotions: prescribed risk-warning wording and prominent placement, 24-hour cooling-off, personalised risk warning, no incentives, appropriateness assessments that genuinely test understanding.

sources.title: Investor awareness messages on trading apps
sources.notes: Regulator circular: brokers must display regulator-supplied investor awareness messages and risk disclosures on alternate days on the landing page of trading apps, in bilingual format, from 1 November 2026.

sources.title: Gamification and retail investing
sources.notes: Regulator research: positive friction before high-risk trades (confirmation step, PIN re-entry, cool-down); gamified features opt-in with informed consent; labels stating persuasive intent.

sources.title: Digital engagement practices: request for comment
sources.notes: Regulator request for comment on behavioural prompts, gamification and design elements on digital platforms; a request for comment, not a rule.

sources.title: Digital engagement practices: Federal Register text
sources.notes: Federal Register text of the regulator request for comment on digital engagement practices on trading platforms.

sources.title: Investment gamification and implications for capital markets
sources.notes: Standards-body report: move away from one-click transactions toward order, review and confirm; plain-language point-of-transaction disclosures; rewards tied to long-term outcomes, not transactions.

sources.title: ESMA agrees to prohibit binary options and restrict CFDs
sources.notes: Product-intervention measures: leverage limits by asset class, margin close-out at 50% of minimum required margin, negative-balance protection, restriction on incentives, standardised risk warning including the percentage of retail accounts that lost money.

sources.title: Directive (EU) 2024/2831 on improving working conditions in platform work
sources.notes: Platform-work directive: automated decisions expressly include pricing of individual assignments and earnings; platforms must disclose the categories of automated decisions, the data and main parameters and their relative importance, in clear plain language; account restriction, suspension or termination must be taken by a human being; workers have a right to an explanation, a named contact and a reply within two weeks; automated systems must not put undue pressure on workers or risk safety; effective reporting channels required; no processing of emotional state, private conversations, off-duty data or biometric identity data.

sources.title: Visual-Manual Driver Distraction Guidelines
sources.notes: Regulator safety guidance for in-vehicle and portable devices: a single eyes-off-road glance no more than 2 seconds, total eyes-off-road time no more than 12 seconds, operable with one hand, limited manual inputs and unnecessary visual information; lockouts while driving for manual text entry, internet browsing, navigation destination entry, 10-digit dialling, more than 30 characters of non-driving text, and automatically scrolling text.

sources.title: NIST Special Publication 1181, Unit Pricing Guide
sources.notes: Standards-body best-practice guide to unit pricing, explicitly covering e-commerce sites as well as shelf labels: one unit of measure for each product category across brands and sizes, unit price shown for every price on offer including sale and multi-buy prices.

sources.title: NIST Handbook 130, Uniform Unit Pricing Regulation
sources.notes: Model unit pricing regulation: uniform units by category (weight per ounce or pound, or per 100 g or kg; liquid per fluid ounce, pint, quart or gallon, or per litre or 100 mL; count per unit), with stated exemptions for very small packs, single-brand single-size lines, and variety and combination packs.

sources.title: Directive 98/6/EC on the indication of prices
sources.notes: Consumer-protection directive on price indication: selling price and unit price must be unambiguous, easily identifiable and clearly legible; prices are final, including taxes; the unit price may be omitted only where identical to the selling price, and only the unit price is required for bulk products.

sources.title: GS1 identification standards: GTIN
sources.notes: Globally unique product identification: GTIN-12 in North America, GTIN-13 elsewhere, GTIN-8 for small packs, GTIN-14 for cases; the check digit catches misreads; a GTIN is never reassigned to a different product.

sources.title: OCPP 2.0.1 explained: key benefits for the EV ecosystem
sources.notes: Open protocol explainer: OCPP 2.0.1 reservation features let drivers book a charging station for a stated time slot, with automatic release of the reservation when the driver does not arrive within a stated window.

sources.title: OCPI Commands: async remote control
sources.notes: OCPI 2.2.1 commands guide: RESERVE_NOW holds a charge point for a token until an expiry time, CANCEL_RESERVATION releases it early, each command translating into the matching open-protocol message to the charge point.

sources.title: Season Tickets | National Rail
sources.notes: Sector information page: season tickets offer unlimited travel between two stations, available weekly, monthly, annually and for any period from one month and one day up to one year, with Flexi Season giving 8 days of travel in 28 days, each travel day activated before use.

sources.title: Season Tickets Terms and Conditions | National Rail
sources.notes: Season ticket terms: refund from the retailer on surrender, worked out as price paid minus the cost of tickets for the period used, administration charge of no more than £10, at least seven days remaining on a monthly or longer ticket or three days on a 7-day ticket, annual tickets with no refund value after 10 months and 12 days, Flexi refunds within the 28-day validity period.

sources.title: Send money (P2P)
sources.notes: Platform design guide for sending money to a contact: recipients listed on the home screen, device-check approval for the transfer, and a short journey from contact to confirmation.

sources.title: What Good Certainty of Payee Looks Like
sources.notes: Design note on certainty of payee: the receiver's account name shown to the sender before the payment is initiated, standard account naming, and confirmation outcomes of match, close match, no match, and check unavailable.

sources.title: Next steps for changes to the driving test booking service
sources.notes: Transport-department consultation outcome: from 31 March 2026 a booked car driving test can be changed at most twice, from 12 May 2026 only the learner can book and manage their own test, and from 9 June 2026 a test can be moved only to one of the three nearest centres.

sources.title: Update on driving test booking rules consultation and reducing waiting times
sources.notes: Consultation outcome summary: 70.7% of respondents agreed only learner drivers should book and manage their own test, and the change limit was set at two, with the area a test can be moved to also limited once booked.

sources.title: Checking in | British Airways
sources.notes: Operator check-in guide: with a boarding pass already held, go directly to the bag drop area with boarding pass, identification and travel documents; at staffed bag drop points get baggage tags and check the bag in, with overnight bag drop at selected airports the afternoon before departure.

sources.title: British Airways Checking-in: A Step-by-Step Guide
sources.notes: Operator check-in guide: self-service kiosks print boarding pass and bag tags after confirming the booking by reference or passport, the tag is attached to the luggage and the bag is taken to the bag drop-off area; staffed desks remain available for help.

sources.title: EN 301 549 v4.1.1 is final: what changed and what it means
sources.notes: EN 301 549 v4.1.1 adopted 24 August 2026 and published 2 September 2026: web, document and software clauses move to WCAG 2.2 Level AA, six new criteria, clause 10.7 on user preferences, clause 12 rewritten, real-time communication widened to total conversation; Official Journal citation expected 22 January 2027.

sources.title: Modern Web Guidance 1.0: the web platform expertise your coding agent is missing
sources.notes: Modern Web Guidance 1.0, stable 10 November 2026: 200+ expert-reviewed guides over 250 web platform features with Baseline compatibility data, a modernisation workflow that scans existing code, and cross-browser stewardship by Chrome, Edge, Firefox and MDN.

sources.title: UI SDK compared with Base UI and Radix
sources.notes: UI SDK 0.1.0-beta.1 (November 2026): headless component behaviours for React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, and web components, with structured tools so an automated agent can read and operate components; beta terms apply.

sources.title: Multimodal design: introduction
sources.notes: Voice-first design for screen-paired voice assistants: core functions usable without a screen, every touch target has a spoken equivalent, the screen never repeats the spoken answer, glanceable layouts readable at distance, contrast and privacy rules.

sources.title: Design guidelines: conversational actions
sources.notes: Design for smart displays: voice-forward design, critical path navigable by voice alone, voice output adapted rather than repeated for the screen, one touchpoint at a time, large text, no critical content at the bottom of the screen.

sources.title: Smart displays
sources.notes: Smart displays are voice-first even with a display; rich responses (cards, lists, tables, carousels, suggestion chips) support voice invocation.

sources.title: Food and beverage ordering workgroup
sources.notes: Standards-body workgroup standardising the exchange of menu and order information between a point-of-sale system and a guest ordering interface (television, tablet or website).

sources.title: Paying menu item transaction services
sources.notes: Charging menu items to a room folio from a kiosk, mobile device or television, with room number, serving period and guest name on the posted charge.

sources.title: Manage billing
sources.notes: Posting charges to guest folios, billing windows, and charge routing.

sources.title: Allergen information for non-prepacked foods
sources.notes: Written allergen information easily available; the recommendations apply to distance sellers as well as in-person ordering.

sources.title: Providing clear and accurate information about prices: summary (CMA209)
sources.notes: Total price up front including mandatory booking fees; running total through the purchase; theatre-production example with a per-transaction fee in the headline price.

sources.title: STAR Code of Practice
sources.notes: Sector code for ticket selling: clear pricing with face value and fees, refund of at least face value where an event is cancelled, transferability, cancellation and viewing restrictions highlighted before purchase.

sources.title: Sale and resale of tickets
sources.notes: Trading-standards guidance: ticket price includes non-optional charges; timings, locations and seat numbers before purchase; restricted views flagged before purchase; transfer and entry terms stated before purchase.

sources.title: Common rules promoting the repair of goods — Directive (EU) 2024/1799 summary
sources.notes: Standardised repair information form (repairer, work, cost, time) given free before a repair contract is signed and valid at least 30 days; duty to repair at a reasonable price within a reasonable time; guarantee extended by 12 months where repair is the remedy.

sources.title: Consumer Rights Act 2015, section 23 — Right to repair or replacement
sources.notes: Repair within a reasonable time and without significant inconvenience, with the trader bearing labour, materials and postage costs.

sources.title: Ecodesign Regulations 2021, Schedule 6 — household dishwashers
sources.notes: Spare parts available 7 years to professional repairers and 10 years for end-user parts, delivery within 15 working days, repair and maintenance information including diagnostic fault and error codes.

sources.title: MCP Apps: How Interactive UI in MCP Works (2026 Guide)
sources.notes: Stable version 2026-01-26 of the MCP Apps extension (SEP-1865): a tool points to a ui:// resource holding an HTML document, rendered by the host in a sandboxed iframe with host-controlled JSON-RPC messaging; progressive enhancement, so the tool stays useful where the interface cannot render.

sources.title: EAA & Self-Service Terminals: ATM & Kiosk Rules
sources.notes: Self-service terminals in scope from 28 June 2025: cash machines, ticketing, check-in and information terminals; closed functionality, so the machine itself must supply text-to-speech, personal headsets, multi-sense time-limit warnings with extension, tactile keys, and an accessibility entry point usable without the feature it turns on.

sources.title: 10 Tips to Improve Restaurant Ordering UX
sources.notes: Fulfilment options stated up front with times and fees: pickup, delivery, curbside pickup, and schedule for later; numbered curbside spaces with a text arrival route; expected pickup time stated at checkout and a ready notification; long waits the most reported curbside frustration.

sources.title: How to Implement Curbside Pickup for a Better Customer Experience
sources.notes: Numbered pickup spaces with clear signage, two-way communication with the arriving customer, a 2-5 minute handoff target from arrival, and contactless handoff with pre-payment.

sources.title: Moxi Booking Flow Enhancements Design Sprint Case Study
sources.notes: On-demand childcare booking: availability shown by day with a full-day, half-day, or extended-care filter; multi-child and multi-day booking in one action with per-child pricing; a membership prompt timed only once a booking reaches checkout without an active membership.

sources.title: ETSI advances digital accessibility across Europe with two standards
sources.notes: Fourth edition of EN 301 549 (published 2 September 2026) announced alongside new EN 303 919 for accessible emergency communications, 17 November 2026: voice, real-time text and video in one session, covering user equipment, communication networks, relay services and public safety answering points; both support the European Accessibility Act.

sources.title: FCA seeks improvement to digital loan processes
sources.notes: Regulator review of digital design in customers' online journeys (July 2025): deliberate pauses before consequential decisions, costs shown before commitment, routes to disclose vulnerability, human support routes, and tested comprehension; findings stated as relevant beyond consumer credit to any firm with a digital presence.

sources.title: Digital design for financial products and services: Consumer impact of sludge, deceptive design, timeliness and simplification
sources.notes: Regulator research note (July 2025): obscured information reduces comprehension, especially of product-specific facts; simplification and timely presentation tested experimentally; excessive friction and deceptive design named as risks to informed decisions.

sources.title: Confirmation of Payee: How to check that you're paying the correct payee
sources.notes: Recipient-name check before sending, as presented by a participating provider: four outcomes - match, close match, no match, unable to check - with the decision to proceed staying with the payer and a warning that a no match may mean the money cannot be recovered.

sources.title: Decision on implementing the CMA's recommendation to remove the Whole of Market requirement
sources.notes: Regulator decision on the Confidence Code for energy price comparison sites (July 2018): accredited sites may show only switchable tariffs provided they display a clear link to a whole-of-market comparison; commission arrangements stated plainly; results must cover enough tariffs for a good comparison.

sources.title: EN 301 549 v4.1.1: 6 Must-Fix WCAG 2.2 Changes
sources.notes: Tracker summary of EN 301 549 v4.1.1: published 2 September 2026, adopted 24 August 2026; Official Journal citation expected around 16 December 2026 per the national disability authority cited, against a later expectation of late January 2027 in another tracker - the citation date is disputed between trackers.

sources.title: Designing the first service patterns for local government
sources.notes: Platform service-pattern work: end-to-end patterns for applying for a resident's parking permit, built from Start page, Confirmation page and Check before you start patterns, with confirmation messages and reminders and a printable temporary permit for immediate use.

sources.title: Online parking permit account
sources.notes: Council permit account flow: register an account, enter the vehicle registration number, upload proof of residency and proof of vehicle keeper, virtual permit valid from the entered date and time, automatic email reminder before expiry, visitor permits, and a phone or in-person route for residents without a computer or smartphone.

sources.title: Digital parking permits for councils
sources.notes: Vendor platform case study: permits linked to the vehicle registration number with no physical display, automatic verification of the registration against the transport authority record, vehicle changes reflected within 15 minutes, and manual review where the automated process cannot resolve an application.

sources.title: USPS API: OAuth, Prices, Labels & Tracking (v3) Guide
sources.notes: Guide to the carrier's official API platform: address validation, prices and delivery standards, labels with barcodes, carrier pickup, drop-off locations, tracking and proof of delivery; labels need enrolment and a payment authorisation token.

sources.title: Buy a Shipping Label in Under 2 Minutes Without a UPS or FedEx Account
sources.notes: Consumer parcel quote flow: origin and destination with box weight and dimensions, live rates compared across carriers with Standard and Express options, all-inclusive pricing, label on screen and in the inbox, pickup booking and one tracking timeline per shipment.

sources.title: How to Send a Package in China: Real-Name Rules, and the Counter Routine
sources.notes: Counter and app sending routine: contents checked and weighed at the counter, pricing by weight, distance zone and volumetric weight with the total shown before payment, waybill details, pickup code for collection, tracking number and live link.

sources.title: TV app quality
sources.notes: Platform quality criteria for television apps: five-way D-pad navigation, no dependence on a Menu button, centre button pauses and resumes with left and right seeking, media controls in the system interface where audio continues after leaving the app, and video paused when the app is left.

sources.title: Use Plozz player controls, Continue Watching, and song identification
sources.notes: Player documentation: playback, audio and subtitle controls, chapters with intro and credits markers, continue watching to resume another title, playback speed, and autoplay settings.

sources.title: Mux Robots, now in your living room
sources.notes: Television player design notes: chapters navigated with the remote's directional buttons, summaries and key moments as shortcuts without leaving the player, translated audio and captions through the track menu.

sources.title: School admissions: How to apply
sources.notes: Government admissions guidance: apply through the local council even for a school in another area, list schools in order of preference, apply a year before the child can start, primary applications close 15 January and secondary applications close 31 October, with a paper form available from the council.

sources.title: Step by step guide to applying online
sources.notes: Council online admissions guide: register with an email address, validation email with a login link, up to six school preferences, supporting evidence upload, application reference number on submission, and change and resubmit before the closing date.
