sources.title: The HHS Section 504 Deadline Moved to 2027. Your Obligations Did Not.
sources.notes: Section 504 web accessibility: the 2024 final rule sets WCAG 2.1 Level AA for the web content and mobile apps of health funding recipients, including patient portals, telehealth platforms, online scheduling and payment systems, and kiosks; the interim final rule effective 7 May 2026 extends the compliance dates to 11 May 2027 for recipients with 15 or more employees and 10 May 2028 for smaller recipients, with the standard unchanged.

sources.title: CCPA fines Rapido Rs. 10 lakh for 'tipping prompts' dark pattern
sources.notes: Consumer protection order dated 31 August 2026 (case CCPA-2/53/2025-CCPA): pre-ride tipping prompts and a price-setting control that steered riders toward higher fares held to be deceptive design; voluntary tipping to be offered only after the journey is complete, under the 2025 aggregator guidelines; corroborated by multiple independent reports.

sources.title: Build for every screen with the latest Jetpack Compose updates from Android Developer Summit
sources.notes: Compose 1.13 stable released 18 November 2026 (BOM 2026.11.01): FlexBox and Grid stable for adaptive layouts, progressive blur and formatted text, polygon shapes and shape morphing, Material 3 1.5.0 stable; Material 2, legacy text-field APIs and ConstraintLayout for Compose deprecated; Navigation 3 version 1.2 with type-safe deep linking.

sources.title: Early education and childcare (valid from 1 April 2026)
sources.notes: Statutory guidance for local authorities on funded early education and childcare: funded hours must be free at the point of use with no mandatory charges (A1.31-A1.38); charges for meals, consumables and optional activities are voluntary and can be declined without losing the place (A1.32-A1.36); invoices break down separately into funded hours, additional paid hours, food, non-food consumables and activities (A1.42); session standards of no session longer than 10 hours, no minimum length, not before 6am or after 8pm, and no artificial breaks inside funded hours (A2.4-A2.5).

sources.title: Sessions, fees, and invoicing checklist
sources.notes: Local-authority checklist for settings offering funded hours: funded hours delivered free of charge without mandatory charges, itemised invoices separating funded hours from paid hours and extras, and the charging and transparency paragraphs of the statutory guidance.

sources.title: Early years entitlement: additional charges, transparency and compliance
sources.notes: Local-authority guidance on funded-hours charges: extras must be voluntary, parents must be able to opt out of chargeable extras, no mandatory charges in relation to funded hours, and costs published with a breakdown of funded hours and extras.

sources.title: Classes and booking
sources.notes: Council leisure service class booking: classes bookable online 7 days in advance, cancellation through the online account, refund or credit where a paid booking is cancelled at least six hours ahead, and a waiting list offered on a first-come-first-served basis when a class is full.

sources.title: Play Fair Policy
sources.notes: Council leisure waitlist and attendance policy: waitlist places allocated first-come-first-served after notification, cancellation at least 60 minutes before the activity to avoid a strike, and three strikes in a rolling 30-day period suspending advance booking privileges for 7 days.

sources.title: Bookings and cancellation policy
sources.notes: Council leisure booking policy: two-hour cancellation notice, three-strikes non-attendance rule removing advance booking for 14 days, and a waiting list that notifies everyone when a place opens, with cancellation of the waitlist place through the online account.

sources.title: Borrowing Policy (revised February 2026)
sources.notes: Public library borrowing policy: a valid card may be physical or a virtual card in digital format; e-cards give access to online resources and holds; most items renew automatically where no one is waiting, with email or text notice on renewal.

sources.title: Circulation Policy
sources.notes: Public library circulation policy: loan periods and renewal limits per format, maximum holds per card, account suspension thresholds for outstanding balances, and borrowing by physical card, app, account number and PIN, or photo ID.

sources.title: Borrowing Policies and Procedures
sources.notes: Public library borrowing policy: loan periods and renewal limits per item type, automatic renewals up to three times where eligible, items with a hold not eligible for renewal, and borrowing privileges suspended at a stated fines threshold.

sources.title: Indian cenbank tightens rules to curb mis-selling by lenders, bans 'dark patterns'
sources.notes: Final conduct directions issued 15 June 2026, effective 1 January 2027: dark patterns banned in banking and lending digital journeys, with an illustrative list of eleven named patterns; consent defaults to refusal and counts only once the terms have been shown; no compulsory bundling of third-party products; interfaces subject to user testing and periodic internal audit; corroborated by multiple independent reports.

sources.title: Windows 11 November 2026 update modernises legacy dialogs and adds a customisable context menu
sources.notes: November 2026 update (KB5132061, 10 November 2026): File Explorer context menu redesigned to open faster with eight entries and user control to remove entries, manage third-party extensions, and restore the earlier layout; AutoPlay and Folder Options dialogs gain dark mode; Magnifier gains per-display zoom and viewport locking; Narrator gains support for reading maths equations.

sources.title: Top 10 Features Every Laundry & Dry Cleaning App Must Have
sources.notes: Granular one-to-two-hour pickup windows, recurring schedules, live staged tracking, upfront per-item pricing, photo proof at handover, and slots blocked once capacity is full.

sources.title: Laundry App Features: Customer, Driver & Admin Panels
sources.notes: Pickup and delivery scheduling fields, staged status from pickup to delivery, capacity-blocked slots, and driver confirmation at collection and handover.

sources.title: SwiftWash Case Study: How We Made Laundry Booking Faster
sources.notes: Three-step booking, transparent per-item pricing before booking, status-first order management, and separate customer and provider flows.

sources.title: Dating App Design: Profiles, Matching and Chat Screens
sources.notes: Profile creation as self-expression with prompts and photo guidance, swipe, browse, and curated discovery, match moment with a first-message prompt, and verification, blocking, and reporting kept central.

sources.title: Matching & Chat UX That Keeps Users Coming Back
sources.notes: Decision-ready profile cards, thumb-friendly like and pass actions, brief match celebration with one next step, empty states with next steps, and safety actions within one or two taps.

sources.title: Best Dating App Designs 2026 — UI & UX Patterns
sources.notes: Swipe card as a binary decision, prompt-based profiles that give something to react to, verification badges, icebreaker prompts, and read receipts as a stated premium choice.

sources.title: Booking Discovery Documentation
sources.notes: Booking design patterns from a government design service: show available slots from the first view, skip to the first available time, minimise steps before availability is shown, ask for an account only after a slot is chosen, and keep every step keyboard-navigable.

sources.title: Booking App UX Design: The Kanga Case Study
sources.notes: One shared availability rule set with a separate focused view per role, slot rules enforced on the server so conflicts are impossible rather than unlikely, and sign-up asked for only once a slot worth booking is found.

sources.title: SpaceOnAi App
sources.notes: Workplace booking redesign: navigation around six primary tasks, recommendation cards with reasoning and availability, one booking flow for every space type, and a dashboard that surfaces upcoming bookings first.

sources.title: Design Critique: NY Waterway (iOS app)
sources.notes: Ferry ticket app critique: route selection without location awareness or landmark cues, fare types without clear grouping, and no schedule or travel-time visibility at ticket selection.

sources.title: WSDOT Ferries
sources.notes: Moderated usability study of a ferry app: ticket purchase was the most problematic task, with an external redirect breaking expectations and vehicle-size wording creating anxiety at the point of purchase.

sources.title: Volunteer Shift Scheduling Software
sources.notes: Visual shift calendar with per-shift caps, self-scheduling shift-first or job-first, reminders, and a day-of check-in lifecycle with walk-up check-in.

sources.title: Let volunteers schedule themselves with the new signup sheets in Services
sources.notes: Volunteer signup sheets showing time commitments, conflicts with other volunteering, and who else is serving at the same time, with household sign-up for family members.

sources.title: Designing a Weather App: UX, Glanceability & Information Design
sources.notes: Weather as decision support: hierarchy by decision relevance, current temperature first, near-term rain next, icons carrying meaning faster than words, and uncertainty shown honestly.

sources.title: 10 Weather Dashboard Design Examples
sources.notes: Weather dashboards must distinguish observed conditions, nowcasts, hourly and daily forecasts, radar estimates, and alerts, each with different sources, update intervals, and uncertainty; progressive disclosure keeps the first screen useful.

sources.title: Event Ticketing UX Research: 3 Key Takeaways
sources.notes: Qualitative study of event ticketing sites (463 participant/site sessions, 2,800+ usability issues, 370+ guidelines): mandatory fees withheld until the cart caused abandonment; group buyers need the party size asked before the seat map and sold-out dates flagged on the listing; a section chosen on the venue map must filter the listings, and a view from the seat helps the buyer decide.

sources.title: Six UX Principles That Separate Good Civic Services From Great Ones
sources.notes: Civic services designed for the hardest case first: plain language, trust built by stating what will happen and when, completion as the measure, and failure states treated as part of the product.

sources.title: Citizen Portal Design: What Government Self-Service Platforms Get Wrong
sources.notes: Portals organised around the resident's task rather than departmental structure: begin a transaction before creating an account, plain-language labels, visible progress on multi-step forms, errors that explain the fix, and save-and-return on long forms.

sources.title: UX Design for Effective E-Government Platforms
sources.notes: Government platforms grouped by service area with predictive search and keyboard navigation: plain language, consistent patterns, and accessibility as a baseline for every service.

sources.title: Best Mobile App Concepts | 7 UI Design Examples
sources.notes: Home security camera concept: one calm live view with the urgent information first, a consistent status language so each camera is identified at a glance, and secondary controls one tap below the live feed.

sources.title: SecureHome Security App
sources.notes: Centralised security dashboard: alerts ordered by severity with location, live previews, and timelines beside each, quick actions on the same surface, and system health stated plainly.

sources.title: Chimera Home Security
sources.notes: Privacy-focused surveillance redesign: local storage of footage, clear live camera access, easy access to recorded events, and dense technical controls replaced with visual footage discovery and plain status feedback.

sources.title: Disney Experience
sources.notes: Audit of a theme-park app: one coherent navigation system with each destination in exactly one place, and a day-of view that surfaces reservations and return windows in time order instead of burying them under promotion.

sources.title: LEGOLAND
sources.notes: Virtual queue feature for a theme-park app: a held place in line with real-time attraction statistics, so guests plan around live waits instead of standing in line.

sources.title: Route+
sources.notes: Concept app for park visits: live wait times with a map, smart routes, and timely notifications; usability sessions tightened map legibility, type scale, and notification wording.

sources.title: Government service patterns specification
sources.notes: Cross-government service patterns: common flows for finding a service, registering, applying, and giving feedback, composed into service patterns such as applying for a permit.

sources.title: Common service patterns for local services
sources.notes: Three levels of service patterns; the top level groups whole services by task - register, check, tell, request, apply, book, update - so services are organised by what the resident needs rather than by department.

sources.title: Citizen portal planning guide
sources.notes: Resident portal scope: a catalogue of matters, one account, forms, payments, reservations, status, and notifications joined into a single path; start from the case path rather than the list of modules; ask for information only once.

sources.title: How weather apps work
sources.notes: How forecast apps present the day: one summary symbol chosen from hourly slots, the hourly forecast as the most useful view, radar showing past observed frames blended into forecast frames, and uncertainty stated rather than hidden.

sources.title: Common Alerting Protocol documentation
sources.notes: Alert messages in the standard alert format: category, sender name, area, timing, and severity fields, supplementing the international alert standard.

sources.title: Common Alerting Protocol and cell broadcast for early warnings
sources.notes: The international alert standard adopted as a telecom recommendation: event type, severity, urgency, geographic area, expected time frame, and recommended protective actions in one message, with a register of trusted issuing authorities.

sources.title: Preorder pickup queue management guide
sources.notes: Pickup process design: confirmation stating the pickup location and time window, a ready message naming the channel, a stated arrival policy for early or late arrival, labelled pickup spaces, and check-in by space number and order name.

sources.title: Reducing wait times for in-store and curbside pickup
sources.notes: Two-way pickup flow: order-ready messages, customers sharing an expected arrival time, check-in on arrival with parking space, staff alerts, and order verification before handover.

sources.title: Drive-through windows: assistance for deaf and hard-of-hearing customers
sources.notes: Legislation requiring establishments with drive-through windows to install ordering assistance equipment for deaf and hard-of-hearing customers at each ordering station and to train staff in its use.

sources.title: Guidance on the use of domestic CCTV
sources.notes: Regulator guidance on domestic cameras: point cameras at the own property where possible, capture no more than needed, use privacy masking, store footage securely and only as long as needed, and tell people cameras are in use.

sources.title: Home CCTV systems
sources.notes: Regulator guide for home cameras and smart doorbells: where footage reaches beyond the property boundary, data protection law applies; capture only what is needed, keep footage secure, and answer requests for it within a month.

sources.title: Virtual Queue
sources.notes: Operator page for virtual queues: a complimentary queue through the app, distribution times shown in the app, a boarding group with a return window, and a notice when the group is called.

sources.title: Virtual Queues at Disney World: Tips, Updates, and FAQs
sources.notes: Visitor guide to virtual queues: confirm the party before the distribution time, places go in seconds, a one-hour return window once called, and no guarantee that every group is called.

sources.title: Congestion Charge payments
sources.notes: Official transport authority payment guide: daily charge with charging hours, a lower amount in advance or on the day and a higher amount by midnight of the third day after travel, Auto Pay, and a warning against unofficial payment sites.

sources.title: London Congestion Charge: cost, zone map, times and how to pay
sources.notes: Consumer guide to the congestion charge: charge amounts, charging hours, payment within three days of travel, and the penalty notice with reduced amount for early payment.

sources.title: London traffic congestion charge: what it costs you in 2026
sources.notes: 2026 congestion charge guide: advance and same-day amount, late amount within three days, penalty notice amounts and deadlines, and the three payment routes including Auto Pay and the official app.

sources.title: A2UI
sources.notes: Project site for the open protocol for agent-described screens: the agent describes the surface and the host renders it with its own native components.

sources.title: Elevating apps: New adaptive quality standards on Google Play
sources.notes: Platform announcement of adaptive app quality requirements: Tier 3 adaptive-ready baseline and foldable screenshots from April 2027, and target API level 37 from August 2027.

sources.title: Document: ariaNotify() method
sources.notes: Programmatic screen reader announcements without a live-region element: announce at any time, message independent of page content, normal priority waits for current reading and high priority interrupts, matching polite and assertive live regions; combine several updates into one message since only the most recent is reliably spoken; live-region announcements take priority over calls made at the same moment.

sources.title: Customizable <select>: now in Chrome and Safari
sources.notes: Native select styling with appearance: base-select in Chrome 135 and Safari 27 (September 2026): the picker list styles through ::picker(select), the chosen value through <selectedcontent>, and Safari 27.2 adds ::field-content for the picked text; support is limited, not Baseline, with the remaining engine behind preferences. Keep the native element for keyboard handling and form behaviour; gate styling behind a support check so other browsers show the classic control; keep meaning in text since the check mark and picker icon are not announced; give options an explicit value where they carry description text; the styled control no longer opens the mobile operating system's own picker and no longer sizes to the longest option.

sources.title: Agent Trust Patterns
sources.notes: Six interface patterns for agents that act for someone, v1 October 2026, updated November 2026: consent by example, interrupt on drift, questions with a shelf life, provenance before an irreversible step, show the track record before delegating, and design for the person on the receiving end; only consent graded Strong so far.

sources.title: Trust
sources.notes: An agent earns each permission from its track record, one kind of action at a time: new agents start read-only, every write asks first, clean runs widen what runs without asking, only a person raises the level, and an incident sends the rule back to asking; irreversible actions always ask.
